Description: The legitimate human or system actor initiating requests to the application.
A threat agent attempting to exploit the system (e.g., via Prompt Injection, Denial of Service, or Data Poisoning).
The centralized gateway or backend service that handles user authentication, request validation, and routing before interacting with the AI components.
Linked attributes: LLM Prompt, Validated AI Prompt, API

Description: The orchestration layer (e.g., LangChain agents) that structures complex queries, maintains context, and coordinates workflows between the user and the model.
The core Large Language Model (e.g., GPT-4, Llama 3) responsible for processing inputs, generating text, and performing inference tasks.
The environment where the LLM can execute code, call internal APIs, or perform actions (e.g., "Plugins" or "Tools") based on its generated outputs.
(Retrieval-Augmented Generation) The repository of proprietary documents or knowledge bases used to ground the model's responses in factual data.
A specialized database that stores data as vector embeddings, allowing the system to perform semantic search and retrieve relevant context for the LLM.
The massive datasets used for the initial pre-training of the base model.
Linked attributes: training set, Training Data, specialized training set

Description: Domain-specific datasets used to adapt the model to specific tasks or organizational knowledge.
Third-party repositories or feeds that supply data for training or updates.
The public network environment. It is explicitly labeled "Untrusted" because data retrieved from here (e.g., via web browsing tools) opens a path for indirect prompt injection.
